leemoor_ranger.text: You bought the Lee Moor lease! Thank you. It's been a company works for longer than anyone alive, and today it's yours to put right.
I'm the ranger. Which is to say, I'm the one who gets rung when a pony falls in the pit.

then.text: Mind the lip of the pit and the notices. The notices are mostly about the lip of the pit.
Topsoil's down on the old tips and the gorse is in. Gorse smells of coconut, which nobody expects on a quarry.
Heather's taking and the pit's gone that silly green. The ponies come down to drink and look smug about it.

else.text: Look at it. A hole in a hill and it's a nature reserve. Don't tell the clay company, they'll want royalties.

leemoor_digger.text: Thirty-one years on the monitors, washing the hill into the pipe. You never get the white out of your boots. My wife says it's in the marriage, too.
They say you're putting it back. Good. I dug it, I'd quite like to see it grow something.
